summary: Beaverhead County, MT lookout on Odell Mountain: camp by 1916, wooden L-4 tower in the 1930s, staffed to 1963, destroyed 1976 per one source; no source describes the summit today.

facts.design: Wooden L-4 tower in the 1930s; 18-foot steel live-in dated 1954 per firelookout.com
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1976 per firelookout.com; no source describes what stands at the summit today

events.note: Camp at the site per firelookout.com; a Dillon paper mentions the Odell Lookout station in August 1916 (August 18, 1916)
Another line being strung from the O'Dell lookout to Wisdom, in a June 7, 1934 Dillon item about new telephone construction
John Bailey appointed to the O'Dell lookout (June 17, 1936)
Henry Tiel of Roundup is the lookout (July 26, 1944)
Pete Haldron, Syracuse forestry student, is the lookout (July 16, 1953)
Work to raise the lookout about 30 feet and build a cabin (Dillon paper, September 15, 1954); firelookout.com describes an 18-foot steel live-in
F.M. radio repeater installed on the lookout to improve radio communication between Wise River, Wisdom and Jackson (Dillon, August 6, 1957)
Forest Service lookout men installed at Bender and O'Dell lookouts (July 10, 1963)
Forest Service trail decision signed June 23, 2016: reroute and reconstruct about half a mile of Trail #3010 to the lookout

notes_for_editor: No built event is written: firelookout.com dates the wooden tower only to the 1930s. The 1954 structure is disputed: the September 15, 1954 Dillon paper plans to raise the lookout about 30 feet and build a cabin, while firelookout.com gives an 18-foot steel live-in. The story reports both. The 1953 Dillon item spells the lookout's name Halleron once (September 11, 1953); the story uses Haldron, as firelookout.com does. The Forest Lookouts page ends with a bare 'Removed' and no date, not used as evidence. Elevation 9,405 ft (about 2,867 m) per firelookout.com could fill elevation_m. Record agency and county match the sources. Two web searches: only the 2016 Forest Service project turned up. No photos found.
